intro: Uganda was nicknamed the "Pearl of Africa" by Winston Churchill. It is home to one of the most diverse and concentrated ranges of African fauna including the highly endangered mountain gorilla and the endangered common chimpanzee.

other.d: fairly small reserve on the east bank of the Albert Nile
with half of the world's population of mountain gorillas, this is the main place to see them

n.es: Parque nacional de la Selva Impenetrable de Bwindi

x.around: The roads in Uganda are bad - you will redefine your idea of what is a 'good road' after a visit. Paved roads are few and far between. If you can rent a car, be prepared for a bumpy ride (and make sure you have a spare). You can hire a ride on a 'bodaboda' - a motorcycle with a passenger seat, but beware that many (fatal) traffic accidents involve bodabodas.
x.intro: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park is in Western Uganda. Bwindi forest is the most popular national park in Uganda. It is famous for viewing mountain gorillas in the wild. The park is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
x.safe: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park is generally safe for visitors, especially those on guided treks, but its remote rainforest terrain and position near the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) border mean that travelers should follow standard precautions.

other.d: a bit off the beaten track, this park is home to the beautiful Virunga Mountains as well as to its own gorilla troop and a range of other wildlife

n.es: Parque nacional del Gorila de Mgahinga
n.fr: parc national des gorilles de Mgahinga
n.it: Parco nazionale dei gorilla di Mgahinga

x.intro: Mgahinga Gorilla National Park is a national park in Western Uganda and the nearest town is . It is one of the only four national parks that protect the mountain gorillas. It lies within the Great Virunga Conservation Area that also extends to Volcanoes National Park of Rwanda and the Virunga National Park of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
x.safe: Mgahinga Gorilla National Park is generally safe for visitors, especially when activities are conducted with UWA rangers and licensed guides. However, its rugged volcanic terrain, dense forest patches, and wildlife require sensible precautions.

other.d: located in the extreme NE corner of Uganda on the South Sudan border. Incredible wildlife here that comes right up to the Apoka Lodge. Elephants, zebras, Nile buffaloes, kobs often visit the lodge.

n.es: Parque nacional del Valle de Kidepo

x.around: Kidepo is remote area with little infrastructure and many hazards. Roads are poor - many routes may have sand, mud, washboards, stream crossings and deep ruts that require vehicles with 4-wheel drive and or significant ground clearance. During the rainy season expert off-road driving skills are required to navigate the deep, slick "black cotton" mud of all but the main tracks.
x.intro: Kidepo Valley National Park is in northeast Uganda. It covers 1436 km² and borders onto South Sudan. Less discovered by tourists, Kidepo Valley protects unique flora and fauna that is quite different from other Ugandan national parks.

n.es: Parque nacional de las Cataratas Murchison

other.d: along the river Nile, this excellent park offers great wildlife and bird watching and is home to the striking and powerful Murchison Falls.

n.es: Parque nacional de las Cataratas Murchison

x.around: Your best bet is to either hire a car or go on an organized safari. Don't even bother hitching or taking a bus. It is very difficult to get around in the park without your own transportation. You might get lucky and have a safari opportunity with someone, but you might not.
x.intro: Murchison Falls National Park is in Northern Uganda. The park covers approximately 3840 km², and the River Nile passes through. Rabonga Forest in the southeast has large populations of chimps and the Nile has a lot of hippopotamuses and crocodiles.
x.safe: If you stay to the roads with a safari vehicle, there is no danger. However do not go off the marked roads.

other.d: has several parts to it, but the main section between Lake Edward and Lake George is a more concentrated version of East African parks as far as animals are concerned, although with less splendid…

n.es: Parque nacional de la Reina Isabel

x.around: An armed guard is needed at all times when on game drives, etc., depending on which parts of the park you visit, it is possible to go on game drives and treks.
x.intro: Queen Elizabeth National Park is in Western Uganda. The park covers an area of over between Lake Edward and Lake George, around the Kasinge Channel connecting the two.

other.d: near the town of Fort Portal is famed for chimpanzee tracking and is highly recommended. Twitchers will know that some of the best birding in central Africa is here too.

x.intro: Kibale Forest National Park is situated in Western Uganda, near the town of Fort Portal, and is famed for its chimpanzees. The park is famous for its chimpanzees, and many people come here for chimp tracking. Some of the best birding in central Africa is here too. The Kasese Crater Lakes are in the area.

n.es: Parque nacional de la Selva Impenetrable de Bwindi

other.d: is a mountain range in south-west Uganda bordering the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is 120 km (75 mi) long and 48 km (30 mi) wide with its highest peak at Mt Stanley (5109 m/16,761 ft).

n.es: Parque nacional de los Montes Ruwenzori

x.around: Everything has to be carried into the mountains, the track is too difficult for pack animals. A typical ratio is six porters per client, with each porter carrying 50-litre plastic drums weighing 22-25 kg. As the hike continues, and there is less to carry, porters start to return back along the track. Clients typically have a personal porter who carries up to 15 kg.
x.safe: The main challenges are the... * Terrain, with extensive sections of bog with thick and often deep and liquid mud to navigate, many steep sections on slippery rocks and mud, and basic wooden ladders to climb up and down. Around a third of the track is thick mud, at least 20 km worth.

other.d: is a beautiful stretch of islands on Victoria Lake with isolated beaches and a bit of jungle. Jungle walks you could easily manage on your own, spending half a day.

x.around: Trips between the islands are by lake taxi. Private boats can also be arranged, but these tend to be expensive (something on the order of USh 50,000 per boat per hour) because of the fuel costs.
x.intro: The Ssese Islands are an archipelago of 84 islands in the northwest of Lake Victoria, Uganda. About 43 of the islands are inhabited. The islands vary in size from less than 10,000 m², to over 40 km long for the largest island, Buggala.
